approach.method_basis: The Parent fits a regularized linear score predictor to accepted molecules using counts of atom types, heavy-atom degrees and element-typed bonds. It selects a scored molecule, retains its surrounding graph and uses a mixed-integer program to construct a small, singly attached replacement tree. The program chooses atoms, bonds and an attachment site while enforcing chemical constraints and exact agreement between the optimized counts and the submitted molecule. Accepted feedback refits the predictor and influences later source selection. This construction works, but its separate count summaries can assign the same representation to molecules with different substitution arrangements and different observed scores.
approach.novelty: Add bond-order-resolved counts of the two endpoint degrees, where an atom's degree is its number of attached heavy atoms. These counts describe whether branching or substituted sites are adjacent, so some positional and branching variants that previously tied can receive different learned predictions. The added counts enter both the existing ridge predictor and the exact integer construction equations. This lineage has only its root so far; no sibling has tested this representation. The experiment asks whether this added structural distinction changes actual construction preferences and can make predictions more useful.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-edf80f0d6f5e produced 1,450 accepted integer constructions with zero discrepancies across its 384 count descriptors, yet only 578 of 1,400 positive predicted source gains became actual gains, and mean actual source-relative gain was negative on three tasks. Its Curate observation identifies unequal scores among molecules sharing the entire descriptor vector on every task. One positional pair scores 0.12407071355114722 and 0.18960077353597476 despite identical existing counts. A read-only recomputation of the Parent trajectories shows that endpoint-degree/bond-order counts separate 556 of 705 pairs sharing the old descriptor vector, including 507 of 625 such pairs with unequal scores and that highlighted positional pair. These are retrospective representation checks on already observed molecules, not new oracle results. The limiting behavior selected for this Child is loss of branching and substitution-adjacency information in the predictor's input. The Parent's macro Top-1 is 0.286518146837627 on its single available screening replica; it supplies no established comparative or three-replica advantage.
hypothesis: Augment the Parent's exact molecular count representation with bond-order-resolved counts of the unordered pair of endpoint heavy-atom degrees, and fit and optimize the existing accepted-only ridge predictor over this enlarged descriptor vector through exact MILP equations.

finding_summary.headline: Degree-pair counts changed construction preferences and raised final scores overall, with uneven task gains
finding_summary.insights:
This closes a specific representational gap: adjacency of branching and substituted sites can supply learned information that changes exact graph construction. The eleven choices between molecules with identical old descriptors are particularly clear evidence, because the added counts alone break those predictor ties. Exact descriptor agreement and correct attachment corrections rule out optimized-to-submitted mismatch as the explanation for the remaining prediction errors.

Predictive usefulness is still uneven. On the same emitted molecules and the same accepted training data, the augmented predictor reduced pooled prediction RMSE from the shadow legacy model's 0.055579 to 0.053050, but increased mean absolute error from 0.024969 to 0.025680. Its advantage in final best score therefore does not establish generally better predictions or search trajectories, especially with only one replica and unscored diagnostic alternatives. The molecular assessment finds that familiar inherited rings still carry many unusual heteroatom-halogen and heteroatom-chain appendages, alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. These richer degree counts do not enforce functional-group compatibility or expand the ring-construction domain. Further evidence should separate reliability across replicas, remaining representation limits, and chemical compatibility; the observed gain does not settle any of them.
finding_summary.results:
The added counts separated 556 of 705 molecular pairs that the parent represented identically, including 507 of 625 pairs with unequal recorded scores. The learned distinctions affected construction: 145 feasible comparisons with the same-data legacy predictor produced 107 strict preference reversals and 11 legacy ties broken in favor of the molecule actually emitted. All 1,450 emitted molecules exactly matched all 468 optimized counts, and every batch completed.

On the single screening seed, mean final Top-1 rose from 0.286518 to 0.296789. Docking increased from 0.189601 to 0.284516, decoration hopping from 0.583606 to 0.589489, and median_2 from 0.175888 to 0.183910. Zaleplon slipped from 0.395373 to 0.394288, while sitagliptin fell from 0.088123 to 0.031740. Mean trajectory AUC decreased slightly, from 0.252148 to 0.250435. Of 1,389 predicted source improvements, 604 became observed improvements, compared with 578 of 1,400 in the parent. Average actual source-relative gain remained negative, at -0.006834 versus -0.006591. Total evaluation time increased from 435 to 714 seconds, including about 43 seconds for diagnostic comparisons.

molecular.headline: Inherited ring frameworks carry exotic pendant groups; ordinary indole amides and alkylated diones coexist with heteroatom-halogen chains.
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and Parent trajectories were read. Every task has 300 recorded molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals, from seed 0; no task lacks trajectories. The products retain recognizable indole carboxamides, diaryl fused diones, biaryl chromenones, quinoline/piperidine conjugates, arylsulfonyl pyrrolidines and oxygen-rich polyacetals. Ring and branch SMILES rates are 1.0 on every task. Aromatic-bearing SMILES rates range from 0.6448 to 1.0, so abundant aromatic chemistry coexists with a nonaromatic polyacetal upper-score series. These are generally medium-to-large, substantially substituted molecules. Diversity is moderate across the supplied collection but much narrower within its upper-score families; much of the visible novelty is peripheral substitution on frameworks already present initially. Conventional alkyl, ether, amide, amine and carbonyl functionality coexists with terminal diazenes, nitrogen/oxygen chains, direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, persulfides and haloalkynes. The Parent comparison shows changes in these appendages and in the relative prominence of familiar families, without a corresponding general shift toward ordinary medicinal chemistry. Every proposal set has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Those are absent SMILES annotations, not evidence that the structures lack ionizable groups or stereogenic centres. Synthetic plausibility and liabilities below are structural judgements, not measured stability, route feasibility or biological activity. Recorded scores are rounded for readability. No reference structures or objective-component scores were supplied, so an unseen target pharmacophore cannot be inferred.

per_task.generated_character: The upper-score molecules are medium-sized indole carboxanilides: a fused pyrrolic aromatic system joined through an amide to a phenyl group, usually with aryl fluorine and methoxy or short alkyl substitution. Evaluation 292 adds an aryl terminal diazene; 297 instead has a sulfur substituent directly on the amide nitrogen. The simpler analogue at 240 retains an ordinary amide, methoxy groups, a methyl substituent and aryl fluorine. The wider trajectory also contains biaryl chromenones and densely oxygenated, nonaromatic polyacetals. Mean SMILES length is 51.2, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9138 and halogen_rate is 0.6897. The indole/amide cores are plausible synthetic targets in outline; the complete diazene-, nitrogen-sulfur- and sulfur-fluorine-decorated variants require substantially more chemical justification.
liabilities: The terminal diazene at 292 and direct amide-N-S linkage at 297 make the complete molecules less conventional than their indole carboxamide cores. Other upper examples add direct S-F or N-S-N functionality; a sulfur-fluorine bond here must not be confused with a conventional sulfone.

Oxygen-sulfur appendages recur in the final material. Together with the unassigned geometry of diazene/imine groups elsewhere, they leave chemical identity, compatibility and isolation questions that the scalar score does not answer.
The lower-score polyacetals contain elaborate oxygen-bearing stereogenic frameworks without explicit configurations.
missing_features: The current upper-score excerpt lacks the comparably successful conventional N-alkyl amide chemistry seen in the Parent maximum. An ordinary secondary amide is present at 240, so the gap is sustained coverage of simple amide substitution within the favorable indole arrangement, not absence of amides.

Different fused-ring heteroatom arrangements and alternative connections between aromatic units are not demonstrated by the cited high molecules. Their value remains untested; the observed scores identify a favorable local family, not a specific missing target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide at 9 scores 0.305105. The less extensively oxygenated indole series reaches 0.352934 at 240, 0.386927 at 297 and 0.394288 at 292. The modified polyacetal at 93 scores only 4.09806e-06, despite its substantial ring and heteroatom content. The observed distinction therefore includes aromatic framework and substituent arrangement, not ring abundance alone. Within the same sulfur-substituted amide series, replacing the indole methyl of 297 with fluorine in 299 changes 0.386927 to 0.204535. The final amino/bis(oxygen-sulfur)-substituted indole at 300 scores 0.127853. More halogen or heteroatom decoration is not uniformly favored. Parent n-edf80f0d6f5e reached 0.395373 with an ordinary N-methyl indole amide. The current maximum occupies a similar recorded neighborhood while carrying a terminal diazene; that substitution is not shown to be chemically necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The trajectory is dominated by large, aromatic diaryl fused dione heterocycles, with a second upper-score family of biaryl chromenones bearing nitriles. The aromatic periphery acquires imines, carbodiimide-type cumulated nitrogen functionality, oxime-like chains, nitrogen-nitrogen links and fluorine bonded directly to nitrogen or oxygen. Evaluation 254 combines a fused dione with imine and fluorinated nitrogen/oxygen appendages; 249 carries similarly decorated aromatic surfaces on the chromenone family. The last molecules also contain oxygen-oxygen chains ending in fluorine. Mean SMILES length is 65.6, aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0, halogen_rate is 0.9621 and cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.631. The underlying ring systems are recognizable, but the dense combinations of heteroatom-halogen and unsaturated nitrogen functionality make the complete products questionable synthetic endpoints.
liabilities: Nitrogen-fluorinated imines/carbodiimides and oxygen-fluorinated oxime-like groups are chemically different from routine aryl fluorination. Their repeated combination raises handling and functional-group compatibility concerns.
The final oxygen-oxygen chains ending in fluorine add peroxide-like connectivity. The acceptable recorded scores do not demonstrate stability or an executable synthesis for these combinations.

Repeated C=N and N=N units introduce geometric possibilities that are unspecified in the cited strings. Cumulated functionality is not automatically implausible in isolation, but these densely heteroatom-substituted combinations are not supported by synthesis evidence.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary realizations of the same aromatic polar substitution patterns are thin in the current high-score excerpt: nitrogen and oxygen are repeatedly supplied through fluorinated unsaturated chains. The missing comparison is a stable, compact functional-group arrangement at those sites, not simply more nitrogen or fluorine.

The upper-score series provides little evidence of new cyclic linkers or changed ring heteroatom patterns. Multiple inherited aromatic families occur, but their pendant-chain elaboration does not establish broad exploration of alternative ring architecture.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.548381; the elaborated relative at 254 scores 0.589489. The chromenone/nitrile analogue at 249 reaches 0.588545, so the upper region is not restricted to the dione core. The pyrazoline/phenol derivative at 20 scores 0.535497, and the quinoline/phenoxy/piperidine derivative at 18 scores 0.536296. Within the late dione sequence, changing an oxygen-chain endpoint at 298 to the oxygen/nitrogen chain at 299 accompanies 0.580425 versus 0.587001. These observations show local tolerance of elaborate polar aromatic decoration; they do not isolate a requirement for any reactive bond. The Parent maximum was 0.583606 on a diaryl dione decorated with amino, thioether and azo functionality. The current upper-score chemistry shifts toward fluorinated imine/oxime/carbodiimide appendages while retaining a familiar ring family.

per_task.generated_character: These are large, heavily substituted biphenyl/arylsulfonyl-pyrrolidine compounds with flexible secondary or tertiary aliphatic amine linkers. The pyrrolidine nitrogen remains sulfonylated; the visibly available amine centres are elsewhere, including linker nitrogens and aniline groups. The maximum at 286 combines an aniline-bearing biphenyl, a tertiary amine carrying a dibromomethyl group, a chlorinated allylic branch, an aryl thiol and a terminal disulfanyl/persulfide group. The other upper molecules repeatedly carry brominated carbon groups, thiols, persulfides and sometimes oxygen-bromine appendages. Mean SMILES length is 81.5, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9759 and halogen_rate is 0.9517. The core sulfonamide/amine chemistry is familiar, but the cumulative size and unusual peripheral combinations make these questionable complete synthetic targets.
liabilities: Brominated amine substituents, chlorinated allylic branches and extensive aromatic halogenation create a bulky, chemically demanding periphery. Direct O-Br groups in some upper examples are distinct from ordinary carbon-bound bromine.
Aryl thiols, terminal persulfides and mixed sulfur chains add compatibility and oxidation-state concerns. These motifs should not be summarized merely as conventional thioethers or sulfones.

Multiple flexible connections, crowded substituted saturated centres and unspecified stereochemistry complicate molecular identity and synthesis. The recorded task scalar is not a measurement of affinity or selectivity.
missing_features: The dominant family does not independently explore nitrogen electronic state and placement: its cyclic nitrogen stays sulfonylated while added basic centres occupy external linkers. A conventional unsulfonylated cyclic amine in this same geometric setting is not shown; its value cannot be inferred from the low-scoring amine-containing alternative scaffold.

Chemically simple matched alternatives to the dibromomethyl-, persulfide- and oxygen-bromine-bearing periphery are not well represented in the cited upper set. An ordinary secondary amine connector does occur at 214, so the gap is retaining useful amine geometry while independently reducing peripheral liabilities.

The substituted saturated ring and branched linker centres are not stereochemically specified, and explicitly charged alternatives are absent from the proposal strings. Evaluation-side protonation or conformer preparation is not documented here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial acid/amide-linked arylsulfonyl pyrrolidine at 10 scores 0.0190412. The amine-linked sulfur-rich member at 210 scores 0.187213 and the related compound at 286 reaches 0.284516. Several structural features change together, so neither sulfur addition nor amide/acid removal can be assigned that gain independently. The bromophenyl diaryl dione at 133 scores 0.000747521. The initial quinoline/piperidine at 6 scores 0.000378699 despite containing an ordinary tertiary cyclic amine, showing that amine presence alone does not explain the gradient. The late pair 296 and 297 changes a larger dithiol-containing side branch to a directly attached thiol on the saturated ring, with scores 0.0991265 and 0.192606. Thus additional sulfur-bearing bulk is not uniformly favorable. The Parent maximum of 0.189601 had a chlorinated enamine linker on the same broad arylsulfonyl-pyrrolidine family. The current upper series emphasizes aliphatic amines and sulfur/bromine-rich decoration; no binding pose or specific receptor interaction is established by these records.

per_task.generated_character: The upper-score chemistry is comparatively conventional: alkylated diaryl fused diones bearing ordinary carbonyls, phenols and short hydrocarbon substituents, alongside quinoline/phenoxy conjugates of N-methyl piperidines. Evaluation 92 combines the fused dione with propyl and ethyl substitution, a phenol and an aldehyde. Evaluation 221 has a quinoline ether, an aniline-linked piperidine, a ketone and an aldehyde. The wider proposal set also repeatedly retains the arylsulfonyl pyrrolidine/acid family. These are medium-to-large aromatic molecules; mean SMILES length is 68.3, aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0, halogen_rate is 0.4862 and cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.0. The principal high-score structures look plausible as medicinal-chemistry starting points in outline, although aldehydes and some bulky alkyl elaborations still need scrutiny.
liabilities: Several upper examples carry aldehydes, which leave electrophilicity and chemical-compatibility questions even when the rest of the molecule uses familiar functionality.
Longer alkyl branches add flexible hydrophobic material without a monotonic recorded benefit. The final butyl/pentyl pair makes that limitation visible.
The piperidine-containing examples leave stereochemical configurations unspecified. Earlier N-O-rich variants elsewhere in the trajectory are less ordinary than the principal alkyl/carbonyl series.
missing_features: The high-score quinoline/piperidine entries do not supply a matched set of less reactive alternatives to their aldehydes. The high-scoring dione methyl ester shows that an aldehyde is not universally required in the observed upper range, but transferring that substitution between frameworks remains untested.

Alternative ring arrangements and defined configurations of substituted piperidines are not represented by the cited upper-score molecules. The modest positional and chain-length gradients do not identify a specific absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.167839; the alkyl/aldehyde-substituted member at 92 scores 0.183910. The quinoline/piperidine example at 221 scores 0.181769, and the dione methyl ester at 239 scores 0.181135. The modified biphenyl/pyran carboxamide at 30 scores 0.105623. Ordinary functional groups are therefore compatible with both higher and lower scores; their arrangement on the ring framework matters. The late dione pair 295 and 296 differs in the position of a phenyl methyl substituent and scores 0.175187 versus 0.180579. Extending the peripheral butyl chain of 299 to the pentyl chain of 300 changes 0.177211 to 0.173640. These are direct examples of position and chain length mattering without a general reward for molecular growth. The Parent maximum was 0.175888 in a quinoline/piperidine aldehyde series. The current maximum lies in the diaryl dione family, while ordinary alkyl/ether/carbonyl chemistry remains present in both panels.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest observed molecules are densely oxygenated, nonaromatic polyacetals resembling protected carbohydrate frameworks. Their periphery contains direct S-F groups, alkynes ending in sulfur-fluorine functionality, N-Cl groups and aldehydes. Evaluation 220 has that combination on the polyacetal framework. Aromatic diaryl diones remain common in the trajectory, and evaluation 129 reaches the upper excerpt with fluoroalkynyl and carbonyl substituents. Mean SMILES length is 57.8, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6448 and halogen_rate is 0.8034: the high polyacetals must not be mistaken for a wholly nonaromatic proposal set. The ring frameworks are recognizable, but their densely substituted heteroatom-halogen and alkynyl periphery is questionable as a stable, isolable synthetic series.
liabilities: Direct sulfur-fluorine and nitrogen-chlorine bonds, fluoroalkynes and alkynyl sulfur-fluorine groups are unusual medicinal substituents whose mutual compatibility is not established by a valid molecular graph.
The crowded polyacetal framework would require stereochemical and synthetic control. The proposal strings provide neither explicit configurations nor evidence of an executable route.

The final aromatic compounds continue to combine sulfur-containing appendages with N-Cl and nitrogen-nitrogen functionality. Their very small scores do not rescue the chemical plausibility of those combinations.
missing_features: The upper polyacetal series lacks demonstrated chemically ordinary replacements that retain its locally favorable heteroatom and unsaturation arrangement without direct S-F/N-Cl or haloalkynyl endpoints. Whether such a replacement preserves any score is unknown.

Configurations of the numerous substituted oxygen-bearing centres are absent. The records therefore do not establish a stereochemically defined series, despite the complexity of the underlying frameworks.

No specific absent pharmacophore follows from these scores: both aromatic and nonaromatic families can enter the upper excerpt, while closely related heteroatom-rich derivatives can score extremely poorly. Missing target chemistry cannot be assigned from the task name.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial polyacetal at 4 scores 2.54690e-05; the substituted relative at 220 scores 0.0317402. The initial aromatic dione at 7 scores 0.00209445, and the fluoroalkynyl dione at 129 scores 0.0158795. The gradient therefore admits more than one ring family. The aryl pyrazoline/thioamide carrying sulfur-fluorine and fluoroalkyl substitution at 184 scores only 3.08411e-39, while the nitrogen-chain-decorated polyacetal at 20 scores 1.16030e-25. Neither sulfur/fluorine presence nor the polyacetal framework alone explains the higher values. In the late polyacetal sequence 295-297, changing the alkyne endpoint gives 0.00159344 for the nitrogen-chlorine variant, 0.00751374 for the sulfur-fluorine variant and 4.65983e-05 for the aldehyde variant. Those matched local examples show a sharp dependence on the particular peripheral group. The Parent maximum was 0.0881235 on a polyacetal decorated with terminal thiocarbonyls, an aldehyde and a trichloromethyl group. The current upper chemistry shifts to S-F/N-Cl/alkynyl decoration and a lower recorded maximum; neither panel supplies evidence of a conventional stable endpoint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-score examples repeatedly carry direct N-F, O-F, S-F, N-Cl or O-Br bonds, nitrogen/oxygen chains, terminal persulfides and haloalkynes. One proposal set has cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.631 and halogen_rate 0.9621; another has halogen_rate 0.9517. At the same time, a simple indole carboxamide scores 0.352934 and an alkylated diaryl dione scores 0.183910 in their respective trajectories. The molecules demonstrate conventional alternatives, but their polar substituents often become elaborate heteroatom chains rather than independently varied familiar functional groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably express new polar functionality as chemically compatible, conventional local groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs local chemical-environment and compatibility control that keeps ordinary amines, amides, ethers, carbonyls and appropriately stabilized sulfur groups available as alternatives. Separate halogen attached to carbon from halogen attached to a heteroatom, and avoid treating equal atom inventories as chemically interchangeable. Preserve comparable ordinary substitutions for feedback to assess; the observed records do not justify declaring a universal score benefit for any functional-group restriction.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate is 1.0 for every proposal set, yet the cited upper molecules remain recognizable derivatives of initial indoles, fused diones, chromenones, arylsulfonyl pyrrolidines, quinoline/piperidine conjugates or polyacetals. The comparison with the Parent mainly changes pendant groups and the prominence of these same families. Ring abundance therefore does not establish broad coverage of alternative cyclic connectivity or ring heteroatom placement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output demonstrates abundant inherited rings but limited exploration of substantially different cyclic architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broader chemical coverage would require a generator domain that can vary ring connectivity, ring heteroatom arrangement and the links between ring units while preserving feasible chemistry. This is a coverage gap inferred from the products, not evidence that a particular unseen ring system improves an objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre_rate and charged_rate are both 0.0 on every task. The actual products nevertheless include substituted piperidines and pyrrolidines, branched amine linkers and elaborate polyacetals with potential stereogenic centres, as well as ionizable amines and acids. Cited imine and diazene products also leave geometric alternatives unspecified. These observations establish absent submitted-state annotations, not absence of stereochemistry or ionization in solution; evaluation-side preparation is not shown.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated structures leave stereochemical and ionization-state alternatives unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the candidate contract permits, express chemically justified stereoisomers and ionization states explicitly and preserve those distinctions in candidate identity. Base state handling on generic chemical rules and observed feedback, without assuming that an annotation itself improves a score.

method_name: Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction
method_thesis: Anchor the method in inverse-QSAR through coupled linear regression and mixed-integer graph construction. [Zhu et al., Sections 1, 3 and 4](https://www.imrpress.com/journal/FBL/27/6/10.31083/j.fbl2706188) encode both a molecular descriptor function and a learned predictor in a program that constructs a graph satisfying structural specifications. Our benchmark adaptation fits a regularized linear score model only to the current objective's accepted observations, using atom-type, degree and typed-bond counts that can be represented exactly by integer constraints. For each proposal, take a scored molecule, choose a bounded editable peripheral region and retain its connected surrounding context. Represent replacement atom identities, bond orders and attachment choices as discrete variables, with connectivity, valence and descriptor-consistency constraints. Maximize the fitted scalar prediction over these variables instead of solving the paper's fixed target-interval problem. A feasible integer assignment supplies the new molecular graph directly. Validate the actual graph and recompute its descriptors before submission; exclude repeated assignments and retry construction when canonical identity is duplicate or invalid. Vary contexts and editable regions as feedback accumulates, and continue construction until the announced batch is filled. Use bounded subproblems and feasible solver incumbents rather than requiring a proof of global optimality for every proposal. The root needs no generative checkpoint or external labels. It constructs atom and bond combinations, without a corpus molecule pool, stored-fragment retrieval or the paper's subsequent isomer-enumeration stage. Each objective starts with clean scored and fitted state. The hypothesis is that jointly enforcing realizable structure while optimizing a task-local prediction concentrates evaluations on improving molecules and raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Exact descriptor realization cannot compensate for an inaccurate predictor; both predictive usefulness and sufficient construction throughput remain unproven.

Feasible source-reference encoding and incumbent decoding with independent sanitization, connectivity, valence, context, descriptor and predictor checks
